name: Plastic drink bottle
instruction: Empty it first. If there is drink residue, rinse it out. Singapore’s recycling is commingled, so accepted plastic, paper, metal and glass recyclables share the blue bin.
tip: A recycling symbol alone doesn’t prove an item is accepted. Check the item and keep food or liquid out.

name: Aluminium drink can
instruction: Empty the can. Place it with other accepted recyclables in the blue bin. If it carries a beverage deposit mark, check the return instructions before recycling.
tip: Food or liquid residue can contaminate recyclables. Empty it and rinse only if needed.

name: Glass bottle or jar
instruction: Empty the bottle or jar and place it with accepted recyclables in the blue bin. Don’t put broken glass in loose where it could injure someone.
tip: Glass cookware, mirrors and ceramics are different from glass containers—check the local guide before sorting.

name: Clean cardboard box
instruction: Flatten clean, dry cardboard before placing it in the blue bin. Remove leftover food or heavily soiled sections.
tip: Greasy or food-stained paper packaging should not go into the blue recycling bin.

name: Newspaper
instruction: Keep newspaper clean and dry, then place it in the blue recycling bin. Wet or food-soiled paper should stay out.
tip: Paper should be clean and dry for recycling.

name: Metal food can
instruction: Empty and rinse the can, then place it in the blue recycling bin. A food can is not a 10¢ beverage-return container.
tip: Remove food residue; do not use the Return Right bottle and can machines for food tins.

name: Plastic food container
instruction: Empty and rinse a rigid plastic container, then place it in the blue recycling bin. If it is foam or heavily food-soiled, use general waste instead.
tip: This advice is for rigid plastic tubs and containers, not Styrofoam.

name: Drink carton
instruction: Empty, rinse and flatten the carton before placing it in the blue recycling bin.
tip: Keep food and liquid out of the recycling stream.

name: Fruit or vegetable scraps
instruction: These scraps can be composted if you have a suitable home composting setup. If you don’t, dispose of them as general waste; don’t put food waste in the blue recycling bin.
tip: Separate food scraps from non-food items before composting.

name: Food-stained paper packaging
instruction: Food-stained paper packaging should not go into the blue recycling bin. Put it in general waste unless your local collection has a specific food-waste route.
tip: Clean, dry paper packaging may be recyclable; food or grease changes the answer.

name: Tissue paper
instruction: Tissue paper is not accepted in Singapore’s blue recycling bin. Put it in general waste.
tip: Not all paper is recyclable. Fibres and contamination affect whether it can be processed.

name: Styrofoam food container
instruction: Styrofoam and food-stained items should not go into the blue recycling bin. Put this in general waste.
tip: When in doubt, keep questionable items out of the blue bin to avoid contaminating recyclables.

name: AA / AAA battery
instruction: Take household batteries to a dedicated battery or e-waste collection bin. Do not put batteries in the blue recycling bin or general waste chute.
tip: Use NEA’s e-waste locator to find an appointed collection point near you.

name: Old mobile phone
instruction: Use a dedicated e-waste collection point or an available take-back service. Don’t put electronics in the blue recycling bin.
tip: Check the collection point accepts phones and remove personal data before handing the device over.

name: Clothing or reusable textile
instruction: Cloop yellow textile bins accept clean, dry clothing and other reusable items on their accepted list. Keep wet, dirty, or mouldy textiles out; check the list before you go.
tip: Textile bins are not the same as donation boxes. Cloop’s white boxes accept only clean, good-quality items; yellow bins have their own accepted-items list.

name: Clean plastic bag
instruction: The NEA guide lists clean plastic bags for blue-bin recycling. Keep the bag empty and clean; contaminated or food-soiled plastic packaging belongs in general waste.
tip: A photo cannot reliably show whether the inside is clean. Check it before recycling.

name: Shampoo or detergent bottle
instruction: Empty the bottle and rinse it before placing it in the blue recycling bin. Remove leftover product where practical.
tip: This guidance is for an empty plastic bottle, not a pump mechanism or mixed-material dispenser.

name: Magazine or brochure
instruction: Keep printed paper clean and dry, then place it in the blue recycling bin. Remove non-paper extras such as fabric, foil or large bindings when practical.
tip: Books in reusable condition can be donated instead.

name: Egg tray
material: Paper or plastic · check the material
answer: Blue recycling bin if clean and accepted
instruction: The NEA guide lists clean paper and plastic egg trays among recyclable packaging. If the tray is foam, heavily soiled, or its material is unclear, keep it out of the blue bin and check local guidance.
tip: The photo may not distinguish paper pulp, rigid plastic and foam. Confirm the material before sorting.

name: Clean aluminium foil or tray
instruction: The NEA guide accepts clean aluminium foil and trays. Empty and rinse them first. Dirty foil or trays with food or oil stains should go in general waste.
tip: Foil is easily contaminated; the item needs to be visibly clean before recycling.

name: Empty aerosol can
answer: Blue recycling bin only when fully empty
instruction: Only recycle an aerosol can when it is completely empty and no product comes out when sprayed. If it still contains product or you are unsure, do not place it in the blue bin; follow the product and local disposal guidance.
tip: A photo cannot confirm that an aerosol can is empty. Check it safely before recycling.

name: Light bulb or fluorescent tube
instruction: Do not place light bulbs or tubes in the blue recycling bin. Take them to an e-waste collection point and handle broken bulbs carefully.
tip: Check that the collection point accepts your bulb type before travelling.

name: Laptop or tablet
instruction: Check whether the device can be repaired, reused or donated first. Otherwise use an e-waste collection point, retailer take-back or an available collection service. Do not put electronics in a blue bin.
tip: Remove personal data and check battery handling instructions before handing over a device.

name: Power bank
instruction: Take a power bank to a dedicated e-waste collection point. Do not put it in a blue recycling bin or general waste chute.
tip: If the battery is swollen, hot or damaged, avoid handling it and check official safety guidance.

name: Ceramic or Pyrex cookware
answer: General waste · not the blue recycling bin
instruction: Ceramics, Pyrex, oven-safe and tempered glass are not accepted in Singapore’s blue recycling bins. Dispose of small items as general waste and handle broken pieces safely.
tip: Heat-resistant cookware is different from ordinary glass bottles and jars.
